identity.name: Uncommon Command on ESXi Virtualization Host — Hypervisor CLI
identity.summary: Adversary in the ESXi hypervisor management plane runs uncommon shell commands (interactive shell, account manipulation, audit tampering, mass-VM impact) that Cortex Analytics flags on the VMware ESXi syslog feed.
identity.description: After reaching the ESXi management plane, an adversary issues shell commands rarely seen on virtualization hosts — spawning an interactive shell, adding a backdoor local account, disabling syslog forwarding to blind the SOC, and powering off / encrypting VMs for ransomware impact. ESXi forwards its shell/hostd command log to a Cortex Broker VM over syslog; the Cortex Analytics per-host rarity model raises 'Uncommon command executed on a virtualization host'. CortexSim reproduces the detectable syslog telemetry with esxi_syslog_emitter.py — no real ESXi is touched.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

execution.framework_reference_id: VMware ESXi syslog data source — 'Uncommon command executed on a virtualization host' (T1059.012 Hypervisor CLI).

prerequisites.description: A Cortex Broker VM syslog applet (UDP/TCP 514) wired into Cortex XSIAM as the 'VMware virtualization servers syslogs' data source. CortexSim streams to it; no real ESXi needed.

payload.code:
# CortexSim ESXi uncommon-command analytics validation — streams shape-true
# ESXi shell syslog records to the lab Broker VM. No real ESXi is touched; the
# attacker commands appear ONLY as syslog TEXT the Cortex analytics model reads.
COLLECTOR="${BROKER_VM:-192.0.2.9}"
# 1) establish the learned-normal baseline the per-host rarity model trains on
python3 core/eal_simulator/esxi_syslog_emitter.py --collector "$COLLECTOR" --phase baseline --baseline-count 40
# 2) emit the uncommon hypervisor-CLI commands that should raise the analytics alert
python3 core/eal_simulator/esxi_syslog_emitter.py --collector "$COLLECTOR" --phase attack

expected_artifacts.description: ESXi shell syslog record for a backdoor local-account add on the hypervisor.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: dataset esxi_syslog: command contains 'esxcli system account add'

expected_artifacts.description: ESXi shell syslog record disabling syslog forwarding (audit tampering).
expected_artifacts.expected_value: dataset esxi_syslog: command contains 'esxcli system syslog config set --loghost'

expected_artifacts.description: ESXi shell syslog record powering off / encrypting all VMs (ransomware impact).
expected_artifacts.expected_value: dataset esxi_syslog: command contains 'vim-cmd vmsvc/power.off' or '.vmdk'

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] ESXi syslog campaign is log-only; nothing to clean up on a host.'

xql_queries.name: ESXi Uncommon Hypervisor-CLI Command on the Syslog Feed
xql_queries.query:
dataset = esxi_syslog
| filter command ~= "esxcli system account add|esxcli system permission set|system syslog config set|system coredump|vim-cmd vmsvc/power.off|\.vmdk|pty.spawn"
| comp count() as hits by agent_hostname, user, command
| sort desc hits

xql_queries.name: ESXi Backdoor Account Add Followed by Syslog Disable
xql_queries.query:
dataset = esxi_syslog
| filter command contains "esxcli system account add" or command contains "syslog config set --loghost"
| comp count_distinct(command) as stages by agent_hostname, user
| filter stages >= 2

products.evidence_query: dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter cloud_provider = "AWS" | filter event_source in ("secretsmanager.amazonaws.com", "ssm.amazonaws.com") | filter event_name in ("GetSecretValue", "BatchGetSecretValue", "GetParameter", "GetParameters", "GetParametersByPath") | comp count() as credential_reads by user_identity_arn, source_ip_address | sort desc credential_reads

threat_scenarios.name: SIM-CDR-020 — AWS credential & secret harvesting behavioral chain
threat_scenarios.description: Validate that Cortex XSIAM cloud-audit analytics flag a single identity bulk-reading Secrets Manager secrets and SSM parameters, and that a correlation stitches the two behaviors into one credential-harvesting incident.

threat_steps.objective: The 'Suspicious secrets dump activity' ABIOC fires on a bulk Secrets Manager read burst by one identity.
preconditions: Collector wired into XSIAM as the AWS CloudTrail (cloud_audit_logs) source.
cloud_audit_emitter plugin registered in the cortexsim EAL simulator.
steps: Stream a SecretsManager GetSecretValue / BatchGetSecretValue burst across many secrets via cloud_audit_emitter.
Observe the 'Suspicious secrets dump activity' ABIOC fire.
success_criteria: The ABIOC raises on the seeded identity within the run window.

threat_steps.objective: The 'AWS SSM parameters retrieval' ABIOC fires on a bulk SSM parameter retrieval burst by the same identity.
preconditions: Collector wired into XSIAM as the AWS CloudTrail (cloud_audit_logs) source.
steps: Stream an SSM GetParameter(s)/GetParametersByPath (WithDecryption) burst across many parameters via cloud_audit_emitter.
Observe the 'AWS SSM parameters retrieval' ABIOC fire.
success_criteria: The ABIOC raises on the seeded identity within the run window.

threat_steps.objective: Correlation CR-CDR-0020 stitches both behaviors into one incident and the validation query confirms the CloudTrail records landed.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs fired for the same identity within the correlation window.
steps: Run the SIM-CDR-020 validation XQL to confirm the emitted SecretsManager + SSM records are present in cloud_audit_logs.
Observe correlation CR-CDR-0020 raise a single credential-harvesting incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-CDR-0020` raises one incident and the validation query returns >= 1 row.

preventive_controls: Scope IAM policies so no single role can read the entire Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store; prefer per-secret resource policies and least-privilege GetSecretValue / GetParameter grants.
Require WithDecryption reads of SecureString parameters to be gated by dedicated roles and short-lived session credentials.
Enable Secrets Manager rotation and CloudTrail data events for Secrets Manager / SSM so retrievals are auditable.
detection_engineering: Baseline per-identity distinct-secret and distinct-parameter access counts; alert on deviation rather than a fixed threshold (the ABIOC anchors to the learned baseline).
Correlate Secrets Manager dumps with SSM parameter retrievals from the same identity/source IP to raise incident severity above either alone.
Confirm CloudTrail control-plane events for secretsmanager.amazonaws.com and ssm.amazonaws.com are ingested into the cloud_audit_logs dataset before relying on these detections.
